newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK ZTS TO INCREASE OUTPUT, BUT NOT WITH ARMS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK ZTS TO INCREASE OUTPUT, BUT NOT WITH ARMS.

text.p: Slovak arms producer ZTS Dubnica a.s. on Friday said it plans to increase annual ouput more than five-fold by the year 2000, as part of a recovery project for the country's armaments industry on the whole.
Historically among the Warsaw Pact's chief armourers, Slovak arms sales and production have dwindled by more 90 percent of the level they were at before the fall of communism in 1989.

In the period after 1989, the country's armaments firms failed in overcoming the conversion shock, as also the workforce in the whole sector was reduced to some 18,000 people, from 80,000 in the mid-80s.
But ZTS Deputy Director for strategy Pavel Motl told Reuters that railway transport equipment and construction machines, and not arms will be the focus of production.

"We plan to boost our production to some nine billion crowns in 2000, from the current 1.6 billion, with the armaments production accounting for a maximum of 20-30 percent of the overall output," he said.
"For example, we are close to signing a contract with German engineering company Krauss-Maffei on cooperation in a railway programme," he added.

Motl said ZTS on Thursday also signed a framework agreement with an unspecified Russian firm, which is, as well as the Slovak firm, seeking to change production away from non-military purposes. He declined to elaborate.

Dubnica, which was badly affected by the halt in production and a conversion programme introduced in 1990, plans to ask the government for debt relief in some form to help. "We are not asking for state subsidies, but we need the state to help in making easier loan conditions with banks," he said.
Dubnica is a member of the new state-run holding company, DMD Holding a.s., with launched its activities in January to coordinate the production and exports of some 26 country's arms producers.
Motl said that each firm in DMD had offered its own recovery and development programme, which the government should review as a whole by November.
"We (Dubnica) drafted 15 programmes, each consisting of several projects, but so far mostly without contracts," he said. "Frankly, we're better with intentions than production at the moment."

Dubnica management recently fell into trouble with the labour unions, after it became public that it intends to sack over one-third of its 5,600 strong workforce, resulting in strike-threats and demonstrations outside the government offices.
"The company will not make massive lay offs, at least until our programmes are reviewed by the government," Motl said.
